title: MongoDB: users batch load keeps records, keys and nesting
summary: Loads 10 JSONPlaceholder user JSON files from a local folder into the MongoDB collection users and checks the result against the source: one document per user record, a unique id and email on every document, and address and company kept as nested documents instead of text.

steps.title: Drop the users collection
steps.explain: Starts clean so every document found later was written by this run.

steps.title: Count the source user files
steps.explain: Each file holds one user, so this is the number of source records.

steps.title: Read sample users (Before)
steps.explain: Shows the collection before the run: just dropped, so empty.

steps.title: Run the mongo_users pipeline
steps.explain: Runs the real pipeline. Everything below checks what it produced.

steps.title: Job finished with status COMPLETED
steps.explain: A finished job should say COMPLETED, not PARTIAL or FAILED.

steps.title: Job processed every source file
steps.explain: The files OpenETL read must equal the files on disk.

steps.title: Count documents in users
steps.explain: The real number of documents in the collection.

steps.title: Documents equal source records
steps.explain: One user record in must be one document out, no more and no fewer.

steps.title: Read distinct values of the id field
steps.explain: A user key must exist on documents and not repeat.

steps.title: Every user has a unique id
steps.explain: Distinct ids must equal the number of source users.

steps.title: Read distinct values of the email field
steps.explain: Email is the second natural key of a user.

steps.title: Every user has a unique email
steps.explain: Distinct emails must equal the number of source users.

steps.title: Count documents whose address is a nested document
steps.explain: Nested JSON should stay nested, not turn into text.

steps.title: Every user keeps address as a nested document
steps.explain: All users have an address object in the source.

steps.title: Read sample users (After)
steps.explain: Shows the same read after the run so the change is visible.

steps.title: Show what the documents really contain
steps.explain: Evidence for the verdict: the actual fields stored per document.
